content:
FINAL JV DEAL DATA SYNC REPAIR — ADMIN → APP → LANDING

Execute now. Do not only hide the NaN values.

CURRENT PRODUCTION DEFECTS

1. JV Deal Management displays $NaN.
2. ROI values are missing in Admin.
3. Admin and public Featured Deals show inconsistent names.
4. PEREZ RESIDENCE is not represented consistently on the public cards.
5. ONE STOP CONSTRUCTORS INC / ONE STOP DEVELOPMENT LLC are being mixed.
6. The admin and public app may be reading different tables or field mappings.
7. Images, locations, developers, categories, capital requirements, ROI, and deal IDs may be attached to the wrong records.

OBJECTIVE

Create one canonical deal record and make every surface read it:

Supabase canonical deal
→ JV Deal Management
→ Featured Deals
→ Landing Page
→ Deal Details
→ Reels
→ Investor Pipeline
→ Documents
→ Investment Flow

PHASE 1 — TRACE EACH CARD

For each visible deal, return:

- canonical deal ID
- database table
- title
- public title
- developer/company
- property ID
- location
- primary image
- capital required
- sale price
- target ROI
- minimum investment
- ownership percentage
- status
- published
- display order
- source endpoint

Trace these three records individually:

1. Jacksonville / ONE STOP
2. Casa Rosario
3. Perez Residence / Southwest Ranches

Do not match records by title alone. Use stable UUIDs.

PHASE 2 — FIX NaN AT THE SOURCE

Find the exact Admin component and formatter producing $NaN.

Audit every numeric field:

- capital_required
- investment_required
- total_investment
- sale_price
- amount_raised
- target_roi
- expected_roi
- minimum_investment
- minimum_ownership
- partner_count

Create one normalization function:

normalizeJVDeal(rawDeal)

It must map legacy and current fields into one typed view model.

Never render:

- NaN
- undefined
- null%
- $undefined

Rules:

Confirmed zero → $0
Missing value → “Not entered”
Invalid value → “Invalid data” and owner warning

Do not convert missing financial data into zero.

PHASE 3 — CANONICAL IDENTITY

Establish the correct canonical records.

Each project must have one:

- deal_id
- property_id
- slug
- official project title
- developer legal name
- public display name
- location
- media collection
- financial dataset

Do not mix:

- Perez Residence
- One Stop Constructors Inc
- One Stop Development LLC
- IVX Jacksonville Prime

unless the database explicitly documents the relationship.

Create an owner review table showing the current and proposed values before overwriting production data.

PHASE 4 — ONE API CONTRACT

Create one canonical public/admin deal response.

Example:

{
  id,
  propertyId,
  title,
  publicTitle,
  developerName,
  location,
  dealType,
  status,
  published,
  displayOrder,
  capitalRequired,
  salePrice,
  targetRoiPercent,
  minimumInvestment,
  minimumOwnershipPercent,
  partnerCount,
  images,
  documents,
  updatedAt
}

Admin and public cards must use this same contract.

Remove separate hardcoded financial mappings and fallback project names.

PHASE 5 — MEDIA AND RECORD LINKING

Verify every image belongs to the correct:

- deal ID
- property ID
- project
- location

Confirm:

- Jacksonville images only appear on Jacksonville.
- Casa Rosario images only appear on Casa Rosario.
- Perez Residence images only appear on Perez Residence.
- Reels use the same deal/property ID.
- The “8 photos” count opens the correct media.

PHASE 6 — EDIT/PUBLISH SYNC

Test:

1. Edit capital required in JV Deal Management.
2. Save.
3. Refresh Admin.
4. Refresh Featured Deals.
5. Refresh landing page.
6. Open deal details.
7. Verify the same value everywhere.

Repeat for:

- title
- developer name
- ROI
- location
- minimum investment
- image
- status
- display order
- publish/unpublish

Publishing must update all public surfaces.
Unpublishing must remove the deal from every public surface without deleting it.

PHASE 7 — REQUIRED DATA QA

For every canonical deal, verify:

- no NaN
- no undefined values
- no mismatched title
- no mismatched image
- no mismatched developer
- no duplicated deal
- no hardcoded financial value
- no stale cached card
- no title-based joins
- one stable UUID end to end

PHASE 8 — CACHE INVALIDATION

After saving or publishing:

- invalidate deal query cache
- invalidate landing cache
- refresh app query
- refresh CDN asset only when necessary
- preserve offline cache but mark stale
- prevent an old card from replacing newer data

PHASE 9 — TESTS

Add tests for:

- missing capital value
- missing ROI
- legacy field mapping
- zero value
- malformed numeric string
- wrong property association
- duplicate title with different UUIDs
- publish/unpublish sync
- display-order changes
- Admin/public parity
- media-to-deal linkage
- stale-cache rejection

PHASE 10 — FINAL PROOF

Return a side-by-side table:

FIELD | ADMIN | APP | LANDING | DATABASE | MATCH

For all three projects.

Required evidence:

- exact root cause
- affected files
- affected functions
- database records before and after
- tests passed/failed
- GitHub SHA
- deploy ID
- runtime SHA
- APK version if mobile code changed
- screenshots of Admin and Featured Deals after repair

FINAL STATUS:

JV DEAL MANAGEMENT AND PUBLIC DEAL CARDS
FULLY SYNCHRONIZED AND LIVE VERIFIED

or

PARTIAL — list every mismatched deal ID, field, image, and data source.
